correctness.rationale: The finite graph has two explicit isomorphic encodings. Enumerating every matching by induction on the first uncovered vertex produces 36 configurations. Exhaustive scanning of all edge deletion sets of sizes 0–5 finds first unique survivors at 4 and 5, 30 versus 6; 240 size-four sets each isolate one of 30 states (8 per state) and each of six remaining states has exactly 22 size-five minimal sets. The independently written LCF program rechecks each matching and every candidate nonmatching subset of sizes 4/5, with corresponding cycle profiles. Both actual standalone programs executed successfully; source files and outputs are embedded.

value.rationale: The dodecahedron is the unique 20-vertex fullerene and a canonical initial case for anti-forcing of molecular Kekulé structures. The literature gives only its graph-level minimum four and a nonplanar counterexample; the natural missing object is the complete profile across all perfect matchings. The classification identifies a six-state structurally exceptional orbit, changes in the number of deletions, and precise minimum-set redundancy (8 versus 22). Those facts supply a reproducible baseline for finer fullerene anti-forcing comparisons and algorithms. It is a coherent natural complete finite classification, not an arbitrary slicing or routine restatement of the known minimum.
